# mongosh

> Use the MongoDB Shell to test queries and interact with the data in your MongoDB database.

- [Release Notes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/changelog.md): Explore the changelog for `mongosh`, detailing new features, bug fixes, and updates across various versions.
- [Configure mongosh](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/configure-mongosh.md): Learn how to configure mongosh behaviors and user experience.
- [Connect to a Deployment](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/connect.md): How to use the MongoDB Shell to connect to a MongoDB Atlas cloud-hosted deployment, a local deployment, or another remote host.
- [Perform CRUD Operations](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/crud.md): Use the MongoDB Shell to create, read, update, and delete documents in a MongoDB collection.
- [Delete Documents](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/crud/delete.md): Learn how to delete one or many documents from MongoDB collections using the shell, with examples for filters, deleteOne, and deleteMany.
- [Insert Documents](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/crud/insert.md): Insert single or multiple documents into a MongoDB collection.
- [Query Documents](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/crud/read.md): Use the db.collection.find() method in the MongoDB Shell to query documents in a collection.
- [Update Documents](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/crud/update.md): Use the MongoDB Shell to update a single document, update multiple documents, or replace a document.
- [Field Level Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/field-level-encryption.md): Configure field level encryption in `mongosh` for MongoDB clusters using various KMS providers like AWS, Azure, GCP, or a local keyfile.
- [Welcome to MongoDB Shell (``mongosh``)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/index.md): Use the MongoDB Shell to test queries and interact with the data in your MongoDB database.
- [Install mongosh](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/install.md): Learn how to install mongosh, the MongoDB Shell, on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Review prerequisites, supported operating systems, and step-by-step installation instructions.
- [Upgrade mongosh](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/install/upgrade.md): Learn how to upgrade mongosh, the MongoDB Shell, to the latest version.
- [Verify Integrity of MongoDB Shell Packages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/install/verify-signatures.md): Verify the integrity of MongoDB Shell packages using digital signatures before installation.
- [Verify Packages with Disk Image Verification (macOS)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/install/verify-signatures/disk-images.md): Verify MongoDB Shell packages on macOS using digital signatures to ensure authenticity and integrity before installation.
- [Verify Packages with GPG (Linux and macOS)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/install/verify-signatures/gpg.md): Verify MongoDB Shell packages on Linux and macOS using GPG to ensure they are valid and unaltered releases.
- [Verify RPM Packages (RHEL)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/install/verify-signatures/rpm.md): Verify the digital signatures of MongoDB Shell RPM packages on RHEL to ensure they are valid and unaltered before installation.
- [Verify Windows Packages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/install/verify-signatures/windows.md): Verify the authenticity of MongoDB Shell packages on Windows using PowerShell or by checking digital signatures in the properties.
- [Shell Logs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/logs.md): Access and manage MongoDB Shell session logs, including viewing, customizing, and setting retention policies.
- [View Shell Command History](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/logs/command-history.md)
- [Enable Log Compression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/logs/compression.md)
- [Write Custom Log Entries](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/logs/custom-entries.md)
- [Disable Logging](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/logs/disable.md)
- [Specify Log File Location](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/logs/location.md)
- [Log Retention](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/logs/retention.md)
- [Modify Log Retention Duration](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/logs/retention/duration.md)
- [Modify Maximum Log File Count](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/logs/retention/file-count.md)
- [Modify Maximum Log Storage Size](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/logs/retention/size.md)
- [View Shell Logs](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/logs/view.md)
- [``.mongoshrc`` Configuration File](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/mongoshrc.md): Customize `mongosh` startup behavior using the `.mongoshrc.js` file in your `HOME` directory, with options to prevent loading or rename legacy files.
- [Reference](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference.md): Explore the reference materials for MongoDB Shell.
- [``mongosh`` Help](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/access-mdb-shell-help.md): Access help in `mongosh` using commands like `help`, `db.help()`, and `show collections` to explore available methods and database information.
- [MongoDB mongosh Cheat Sheet](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/cheatsheet.md): A quick reference of common methods for MongoDB Shell.
- [Compatibility Changes with Legacy mongo Shell](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/compatibility.md): Explore the differences between mongosh and the legacy mongo shell, including deprecated methods, read and write preference behaviors, and data type handling.
- [Configure Settings Using the API](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/configure-shell-settings-api.md): Configure and manage `mongosh` settings using the `config` API to persist changes across sessions, including setting properties like logging and telemetry.
- [Configure Settings Using a Configuration File](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/configure-shell-settings-global.md): Configure `mongosh` settings using a YAML configuration file to apply settings like `displayBatchSize` at startup, with options to override using a config API.
- [Configure Settings](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/configure-shell-settings.md): Configure `mongosh` settings to specify shell behaviors, including logging, telemetry, and history management, using a config API or a global config file.
- [Customize the :binary:`~bin.mongosh` Prompt](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/customize-prompt.md): Customize the `mongosh` prompt to display dynamic session information, such as line numbers, database and hostname, or system uptime and document count.
- [Data Types](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/data-types.md): Explore MongoDB's BSON-supported data types, including Date, ObjectId, Double, Int32, Long, Decimal128, and Timestamp, with examples and type checking methods.
- [Use an Editor for Commands](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/editor-mode.md): Learn to use external or built-in editors in mongosh for multiline command editing, including setting up and using editors like vi, nano, or Visual Studio.
- [EJSON](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/ejson.md)
- [EJSON.deserialize()](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/ejson/deserialize.md)
- [EJSON.parse()](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/ejson/parse.md)
- [EJSON.serialize()](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/ejson/serialize.md)
- [EJSON.stringify()](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/ejson/stringify.md)
- [Methods](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/methods.md): Explore the available methods in the MongoDB Shell, including administration, bulk operations, collection management, with detailed descriptions and usage.
- [Options](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/options.md): Explore options to control MongoDB Shell, including general, stable API, connection, authentication, session, and client-side field level encryption options.
- [Run Aggregation Pipelines](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/run-agg-pipelines.md): Run aggregation pipelines in MongoDB Shell to transform documents into aggregated results using various stages like grouping, filtering, and sorting.
- [Run Commands](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/run-commands.md): Use run commands in the MongoDB Shell to create or switch databases, terminate a query, or clear the console.
- [Snippets](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/snippets.md): Explore how to use, create, and manage snippets in `mongosh` for data manipulation and administrative tasks.
- [Snippet Commands](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/snippets/commands.md): Explore available commands for managing snippets, including installing, listing, and updating snippets in the MongoDB Shell.
- [Configuration Options](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/snippets/configuration.md): Configure `mongosh` snippet settings, including autoload and registry URLs, using the `config.set` method.
- [Error Handlers](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/snippets/error-handlers.md): Explore how to use error handlers with regular expressions to catch runtime errors and display custom messages in MongoDB Shell.
- [Create and Share Snippets](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/snippets/packages.md): Learn how to create, package, and share MongoDB shell snippets, including preparing files, publishing to a registry, and contributing to the community.
- [Snippets Reference](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/snippets/reference.md): Explore available commands for working with snippets in `mongosh`, including package management and error handling options.
- [Registries and Registry Configuration](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/snippets/registries-config.md): Configure your system to use different registries for MongoDB snippets, including community, private, and multiple registries.
- [Create a Registry Index File Manually](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/snippets/registry-index.md): Learn how to manually create a registry index file for MongoDB Shell snippets using TypeScript.
- [Troubleshooting](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/snippets/troubleshooting.md): Troubleshoot common issues with MongoDB Shell snippets, including viewing npm logs and resolving module errors.
- [Use Snippets in the Console](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/snippets/working-with-snippets.md): Learn how to install, run, and manage snippets in the `mongosh` console, including searching for available snippets and getting help for specific ones.
- [Configure Telemetry Options](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/telemetry.md): Configure telemetry options in `mongosh` to manage anonymous usage data collection, with options to enable or disable it at any time.
- [Write Scripts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md): Write scripts for the MongoDB Shell that modify data in MongoDB or perform administrative operations.
- [Script Considerations](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts/considerations.md): Use async functions, async generator functions, or `.map()` for database query results in scripts. Class constructors and non-async generators are unsupported.
- [Use Environment Variables in MongoDB Shell Scripts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts/env-variables.md): Learn how to use environment variables in MongoDB Shell scripts.
- [Include External Files and Modules in Scripts](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts/require-external-modules.md): Learn how to include external files and modules in `mongosh` scripts using the `require()` function for local files, built-in Node.js modules, and npm modules.
- [Differences Between require() and load()](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts/require-load-differences.md): Understand the differences between `require()` and `load()` in mongosh scripts, including their availability, file path handling, and packaging considerations.
- [Code Scoping](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts/scoping.md): Learn how to manage code scope in `mongosh` to prevent global scope collisions by wrapping functions and variables within an anonymous function.
